seo.title: Hotel Revenue Management Company | RateHarbor
seo.description: Hotel revenue management from RateHarbor: meet the company, see who we are and how we work, and send an enquiry to discuss your property.

mainEntity.name: Do you take over pricing and distribution day to day, or do you advise my own staff who keep doing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: We take over the day-to-day work as your outsourced revenue management and OTA management team. Our revenue management service covers pricing and rate strategy, demand forecasting, competitive set monitoring and regular performance reports for you as the owner. Our OTA management service runs your listings and rates on Booking.com, Expedia and other online travel agencies. That includes your content, rate parity and channel manager settings.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with small independent motels, or only with larger branded hotels?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we work with small independent motels as well as larger hotels. We support any kind of lodging property, including hotels, boutique hotels, B&Bs, serviced apartments and short-term rentals.

mainEntity.name: Do you take on properties anywhere, or only in certain regions?

acceptedAnswer.text: We work in many countries, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia, so our service isn't tied to one region. We support independent hotels and small hotel groups entirely remotely. We work in your hotel's own systems and online accounts, and we have no on-site staff at any property.

mainEntity.name: Do you also handle operations like housekeeping and staffing, or only revenue?

acceptedAnswer.text: We handle revenue management, OTA management and related online services. We don't handle hotel operations such as housekeeping or staffing. You can hire us for revenue management or OTA management on its own, or use both together.

hero.heading: Your revenue team, without the extra desk
lead: RateHarbor handles your hotel revenue management remotely, inside your own systems and accounts, while you run the property.

blocks.heading: An Outsourced Revenue Management Company for Hotel Owners
paragraphs: You get an outsourced revenue team, not software you have to run yourself. At RateHarbor, we provide hotel revenue management and OTA management for hotel owners. Our people study your data, build your strategy and do the day-to-day work.

You can hire us for either service on its own or combine them with related online services. We handle your revenue and online distribution work. We don't run your hotel operations. We shape your service around your property, and it grows with you as you add rooms or properties.

blocks.heading: How We Work as Your Remote Revenue Management Consultant

items.heading: Experienced account ownership
paragraphs: Our [Canadian team](/about-us/) has 12 people. Your dedicated specialist has at least 5 years of revenue and OTA experience with independent and boutique hotels and manages no more than 10 properties. The team supports them all 365 days of the year.

items.heading: Remote working rhythm
paragraphs: Through [our remote process](/our-process/), we work directly in your hotel's systems and online accounts, with no on-site staff. We make pricing decisions every day and go through strategy with you on a weekly or monthly call.

items.heading: Evidence before commitment
paragraphs: If you ask before you sign, we share [full case studies](/case-studies/) showing before-and-after RevPAR, occupancy and ADR for properties of a similar type and size. We also share an anonymised monthly performance report.

items.heading: Controlled data access
paragraphs: Under [our data safeguards](/privacy-policy/), we sign your NDA or our processing agreement before we get any access. We apply PIPEDA, plus GDPR and UK GDPR where they apply. Guest data stays in your systems, only our team can access cloud working files, and no subcontractor gets access.

items.heading: Flexible managed plans
paragraphs: Under [our plan terms](/terms-and-conditions/), you can stop any managed plan at the end of any month if you tell us in writing before that month ends. There's no long-term lock-in and there are no cancellation fees. If you cancel during onboarding, you pay only for the onboarding work we've already completed.

blocks.heading: Revenue Management Services, from Daily Pricing to Owner Reports
paragraphs: We take responsibility for your revenue work from strategy through implementation and ongoing optimisation, so you don't have to build an in-house revenue team.

items.heading: Strategy agreed with you
paragraphs: We build your revenue strategy around your hotel or resort and the occupancy, ADR and RevPAR goals you set. Then we turn our findings into improvement plans you can act on.

items.heading: Clear decision boundaries
paragraphs: On the monthly retainer, we decide daily rates, restrictions and inventory within guardrails we agree with you. You keep full control of pricing, see every rate and channel and make major decisions together with us, and we never overwrite a manual rate override you set.

items.heading: Competitive market monitoring
paragraphs: We track your competitive set alongside market trends. That way your pricing and rate strategy is based on competitor benchmarks and demand signals instead of your property's performance in isolation.

items.heading: Daily pricing
paragraphs: On the monthly retainer, we decide rates, restrictions and inventory for every room type, using the pricing approach set out in [Dynamic Pricing Strategy](/dynamic-pricing-strategy/). We respond in real time to pickup, booking pace, seasonality, events and demand. We use targeted tactics when demand is low and set ADR goals for peak demand.

items.heading: Hotel Distribution
paragraphs: With [Hotel Distribution](/hotel-distribution/), we allocate your inventory across OTAs, the GDS and direct channels, weighing booking trends against commissions. We control availability and pricing to keep rate parity and reduce your overbooking risk.

items.heading: OTA listing management
paragraphs: Our [OTA management service](/ota-optimization/) runs your listings and rates on Booking.com, Expedia and other online travel agencies. This covers your listing content, rate parity and channel manager settings.

items.heading: Property-based demand forecasts
items.text: We project your occupancy and revenue from your booking history, current pace and market trends. These projections take into account demand, seasonality and where you stand against competitors.

items.heading: Weekly owner reporting
items.text: Every week, you get pace and pickup reports that compare bookings with last year and with budget. You also get demand forecast reports and a pace analysis dashboard.

items.heading: Forecast checks and corrections
items.text: We deliver monthly and quarterly forecasts, analyse pickup trends and regularly compare actual results with forecasts. When demand runs ahead of or behind forecast, we correct your pricing and plans.

items.heading: Historical data limits
items.text: Forecast accuracy depends on clean historical data. If your property is new or has poor records, your first projections are less reliable.

items.heading: Commercial Strategy budgets
items.text: With [Commercial Strategy](/commercial-strategy/), we build your annual budget by month and segment using planning tools and annual templates. Then we maintain and update your budgets and reporting.

items.heading: Standalone fixed-scope, fixed-fee audits
items.text: We quote [Revenue Management Audits](/revenue-management-audit/) after your free 30-minute consultation. For a single property, we deliver within 10 business days of getting your data and access. Each batch of up to 5 properties adds another 10 business days. Remote training and handover are included.

items.heading: Room-count pricing tiers
items.text: Our [monthly revenue management plans](/request-a-quote/) are priced by room count: 40 rooms or fewer, 41 to 120 rooms, and more than 120 rooms.

blocks.heading: Properties We Support, from Motels to Growing Hotel Groups

items.heading: Independent and boutique hotels
paragraphs: We build your strategy around your type of property. Demand patterns, length of stay and channel mix differ between independent hotels, boutique hotels and resorts, so one standard approach leaves revenue on the table.

items.heading: Growing hotel groups
paragraphs: We take your group's decision-making structure into account, as well as its properties. A tailored strategy takes more setup and discovery work at the start than applying a standard template.

items.heading: Lodging beyond traditional hotels
paragraphs: We work with any kind of lodging property, including motels, B&Bs, serviced apartments and short-term rentals. Our service isn't limited to larger hotels.

seo.description: Hotel digital marketing that grows direct bookings: brand and website builds, Google Ads and metasearch in accounts you own, plus email and social.

jsonLd.name: Hotel Digital Marketing for Direct Bookings
jsonLd.description: Every week, we point promotions and advertising at stay dates that are forecast below 70% occupancy or are pacing behind last year.
jsonLd.serviceType: Hotel Digital Marketing for Direct Bookings

mainEntity.name: What will my team need to give you, such as account access and brand assets? And which ads and content do I have to approve, and how often?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll give us your property details, logo, brand guidelines and photo library. You'll also give us user access to your website, booking engine, email platform and the ad accounts your property owns, and join us for a 60-minute kickoff call. No ad, listing text or other content goes live until you've approved it in writing. We send you one batch to approve each week and ask you to reply within 2 business days.

mainEntity.name: Which choices change your marketing service fee: managed channels, media spend, content volume, website scope, integrations or language versions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your fixed monthly retainer depends on how many channels we manage and how much content we produce each month. Website projects, system integrations and extra language versions are one-time fees, set out in your written proposal. Media spend doesn't change our fee. You pay ad and metasearch platforms directly with your own payment method, separately from our fee, and we take no percentage.

mainEntity.name: Can we commission selected marketing channels without buying the full marketing service or your revenue management service?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can commission paid search, SEO, email or any other single channel without taking full marketing or revenue management. Revenue management, OTA management and our related online services are available separately or together. If you choose several, we bundle them and give you priority turnaround.

mainEntity.name: If you build me a new direct-booking website, how long until it is live, and how soon do campaigns start?

acceptedAnswer.text: We launch a new direct-booking website, or updates to your existing site, in 4 to 6 weeks. Nothing is published until you've signed it off in writing. Ad campaigns start within 10 business days of us getting account access and your approval. Until launch they run against your current site. Bookings traced to paid search and SEO showed within 60 to 90 days for 5 of the 7 hotels we ran both for in 2025; SEO rankings, tracked weekly on fixed searches, usually keep building for 6 to 12 months. We don't guarantee results.

mainEntity.name: What minimum media budget is needed for you to manage paid search or metasearch meaningfully, and which would you recommend if we cannot fund both?

acceptedAnswer.text: For paid search, your budget needs to cover about 30 clicks a day on your key search terms. For metasearch, it needs to keep bids live every day across at least 90 days of stay dates. We launch either channel only when the funding keeps it running without gaps. If you fund one channel, metasearch comes first and paid search second. Metasearch reaches travellers who are already comparing rates, and your spend follows actual clicks or bookings. You pay media spend directly to each platform, outside our fee.

mainEntity.name: Can you take over our existing advertising accounts and campaigns while preserving their history and working around channels still managed by our current agency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You add a named login for us to your existing ad and metasearch accounts, which preserves your campaign history, conversion data and bidding history. We review the accounts for 1 to 2 weeks before we change anything. Where your agency keeps some channels, we agree in writing at the start who owns each channel and task, and we work alongside them to minimise disruption.

mainEntity.name: Which languages can you support for campaigns, website content and guest emails, including localisation rather than translation alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: We create campaigns, website content and guest emails in both English and French. We write and adapt each one for its market instead of translating word for word. For other languages, you supply the translations, and we adapt the layouts, currencies, date formats and offers to the market.

mainEntity.name: After launch or optimisation, do you maintain website content, software and booking links, or must our team or web developer handle those tasks?

acceptedAnswer.text: While your monthly programme runs, we maintain your website through the user access you give us. That covers up to 4 content updates a month, software and plugin updates within 5 business days of their release, and a check of your booking-engine links once a week. If you keep a developer or agency, we agree in writing at the start who owns each task.

hero.heading: Hotel Digital Marketing for Direct Bookings
lead: We run Google Ads, metasearch, email and social for your hotel, spending only on nights still to fill.

cta.label: Talk to us about hotel digital marketing

blocks.heading: Digital Marketing Built Around Your Guests and Occupancy
paragraphs: Every week, we point promotions and advertising at stay dates that are forecast below 70% occupancy or are pacing behind last year. Your occupancy forecast, booking pace and open room inventory decide where our hotel digital marketing puts that spend. Once a date passes 90% forecast occupancy, or fewer than 3 rooms per type remain, we cut or pause advertising for that date and let pricing capture the demand.
We build your strategy around your hotel and the guests you want to attract. We map how those guests book online and optimise your digital channels around those sales funnels.

blocks.heading: Your Digital Marketing Agency, Consultant or Interim Lead
paragraphs: At the start, we put in writing who owns each channel and each task.

items.heading: Consulting or interim leadership
paragraphs: With marketing consulting, we provide strategy, recommendations and training, and your team runs the campaigns. As your interim marketing lead for 3 to 6 months, we set priorities, brief your staff and agencies, and review their work.

items.heading: Managed marketing delivery
paragraphs: We build, run and report on your campaigns ourselves. Your team keeps the final say on everything that gets published.

items.heading: Revenue before traffic
paragraphs: We judge your marketing on direct booking revenue after cancellations, commissions and acquisition costs, not on traffic or gross bookings. Every report leads with direct booking revenue and shows it next to media spend, conversion rate, cost per direct booking and the OTA commission you avoided.

items.heading: Boutique hotel consulting
paragraphs: [Boutique Hotel Consulting](/boutique-hotel-consulting/) focuses your marketing on retail and leisure direct bookings. We advise on group strategy while your sales director handles day-to-day sales. For openings and repositioning, we support you up to 6 months before launch and use market data until your own bookings and guest list build up.

items.heading: Channel performance comparisons
paragraphs: For each channel, we show you revenue both gross and net of OTA commissions, advertising, booking-engine and other acquisition costs, compared with last year, your budget and your competitive set. That way you can tell real net growth apart from bookings that just moved between channels, and the effect of marketing apart from the hotel's overall performance.

items.heading: Audit and strategy deliverables
paragraphs: Our audit gives you written findings and an action plan that ranks fixes by expected impact and effort. The strategy adds a 12-month campaign calendar and a recommended budget split across paid search, metasearch, SEO, email and social media.

items.heading: Our company background
paragraphs: At [RateHarbor](/about-us/), we provide hotel owners with outsourced hotel revenue management and OTA management services.

blocks.heading: A Brand and Website Built to Win Direct Bookings

items.heading: Consistent hotel identity
paragraphs: We develop your hotel's brand identity and messaging, so guests see your property presented the same way on every channel.

items.heading: More direct guests
paragraphs: We audit and optimise your existing website or build you a direct-booking site. That brings in more visitors and turns more of them into guests, so you pay less in OTA commissions.

items.heading: Improve sound foundations
paragraphs: If your current site loads on mobile in under 3 seconds, its CMS can still be updated and its booking-engine connection works cleanly, we improve the site you have. The speed, room-page, call-to-action and booking-path fixes then go live within 4 to 6 weeks.

items.heading: Rebuild obstructive platforms
paragraphs: If your site isn't mobile-friendly, can't hold a booking widget or needs more than half its pages redone, we recommend a rebuild. The extra work lets us redesign the whole booking journey, which in our experience gives a bigger lift in conversion.

items.heading: Booking engine included
paragraphs: A new website comes with choosing, setting up and tuning your booking engine, or with connecting the engine you already use. We don't just add a booking link.

items.heading: Reservations tested before launch
paragraphs: We make test reservations on desktop and mobile and follow each one through to the confirmation emails. We check rates and availability against your channel manager, then cancel every test booking.

items.heading: Find booking drop-offs
paragraphs: Using your website analytics and booking-engine reports, we trace your booking journey from date search to payment and find where visitors leave.

items.heading: Test conversion improvements
paragraphs: We test changes like fewer form fields, clearer rates or more visible booking buttons, and we run each version for at least 4 weeks or 1,000 visits. We keep the version that converts better and then fix the next drop-off.

blocks.heading: Google Ads, Metasearch and SEO in Accounts You Own

items.heading: Google Ads campaigns
items.text: We plan your digital advertising and run Google Ads campaigns that send visitors to your hotel's website.

items.heading: Hotel metasearch campaigns
items.text: We also run hotel metasearch campaigns as part of your digital advertising programme.

items.heading: Brand bidding tests
items.text: In selected periods, we pause your brand campaigns for 2 to 4 weeks and compare total direct bookings. This tells us whether bidding wins reservations you would otherwise lose to resellers.

items.heading: Spend follows booking value
items.text: We keep brand bidding only where resellers are bidding. Where your organic listings win the bookings, we reduce or stop brand spend and move that money into non-brand search and metasearch.

items.heading: Your advertising accounts
items.text: Your ad and metasearch accounts are opened in your property's name and stay yours. You pay the platforms directly with your own payment method.

items.heading: Your digital assets
items.text: Your website, domain and guest email lists are registered to you or kept in your systems. You own all the content and accounts we build.

items.heading: Files handed over
items.text: Within 10 business days after our engagement ends, we give your team the current files.

items.heading: Distribution and channel returns
paragraphs: Through [Hotel Distribution](/hotel-distribution/), we allocate your inventory across OTAs, the GDS and direct channels based on booking trends and returns after commission. You keep your third-party visibility and bookings, and we control pricing and availability to lower your overbooking risk and keep rate parity.

items.heading: Search foundations
paragraphs: We plan and run SEO for your hotel's name, your visibility on Google Maps and your website's technical requirements.

items.heading: Destination and property searches
paragraphs: We also target non-brand searches for your destination and property type, and each target search gets its own landing page. You get 3 to 5 pages in the first 3 months, and we add more as new opportunities come up.

items.heading: OTA and metasearch visibility
paragraphs: Through [OTA Optimization](/ota-optimization/), we aim for a 100% listing content score. We send your rates and availability directly to Google free booking links, Hotel Ads, trivago, TripAdvisor and Kayak, and we manage your Google Business Profile and your reviews.

blocks.heading: Email, Content and Social Media That Bring Guests Back

items.heading: Guest segments and sequences
paragraphs: We grow your guest email list and divide it into segments. We time campaigns to booking windows and build upselling and automated sequences that fill quiet periods without cutting rates.

items.heading: Campaign creation and approval
paragraphs: We write and design each email campaign and send it from your own platform once you've approved it in writing.

items.heading: Testing and monthly reporting
paragraphs: We test subject lines and send times and report your opens, clicks and bookings each month. If your team runs email instead, we give you the strategy and templates.

items.heading: Social media management
paragraphs: We manage organic posts and community replies on Facebook, Instagram and X (Twitter). We also run paid social campaigns in your property's ad accounts, and you pay the media spend directly.

items.heading: Monthly content volume
paragraphs: Each month, we produce 2 website articles of about 1,000 words, 12 social posts and 2 videos of up to 60 seconds. You can commission extra blocks of the same size.

items.heading: Remote video production
paragraphs: We only work remotely. We edit videos from footage and photos you send us or from a shoot you arrange locally.

items.heading: Influencer delivery and tracking
paragraphs: We shortlist creators and agree with each one which posts, stories or videos they'll deliver. Then we check what they publish against those commitments and track the bookings that come from it through a unique booking link or promo code for each creator.

items.heading: Hosted stays and approval
paragraphs: Your property hosts each influencer stay, and you approve every creator before we confirm what they've agreed to deliver.

blocks.heading: Independent Hotels and Small Groups We Work With
paragraphs: We work with independent hotels and small hotel groups. We manage your website, booking engine, digital campaigns and email platforms together as one direct-booking system.
Just ask and we'll share our full [case studies](/case-studies/).

blocks.heading: Booking Tracking That Credits Traceable Reservations
paragraphs: Before we increase your ad spend, we check that completed, uncancelled reservations can be traced back to the campaigns that produced them. We don't judge performance on clicks alone. Some bookings can't be traced, for example when a guest declines tracking or no campaign led to the booking. Our reports list those as unattributed, and we mark which figures come from your booking engine, which from the ad platforms' own attribution and which are estimates.

items.label: Named login access
items.detail: We work through a named login in your own analytics, advertising and booking-engine accounts.

items.label: Cross-domain GA4 tracking
items.detail: We set up cross-domain tracking in Google Analytics 4 between your website and your booking engine.

items.label: Conversions to ad platforms
items.detail: We pass booking-confirmation conversions to Google Ads and metasearch, and link each metasearch platform's tracking to your booking engine, with cancellations taken out.

items.label: Test booking confirmed
items.detail: If your booking engine vendor has to install the tags, we provide the code and confirm a test booking within 5 business days.

items.label: 30-day check report
items.detail: We report impressions, clicks, completed direct bookings and the commission saved compared with getting the same bookings through OTAs, with untraceable bookings listed apart.

blocks.heading: Works With Your CMS, PMS and Email Platform

items.heading: Your existing systems
paragraphs: We work inside your CMS, whether that's WordPress, Squarespace or Wix, and with your booking engine, PMS and channel manager, including SiteMinder and Cloudbeds. We replace a website or engine only in a project you approve in writing.

items.heading: Email platform options
paragraphs: We set up and manage Mailchimp, Klaviyo, HubSpot, Brevo or a comparable platform. We can also use the email tool or CRM you already have, or your PMS's guest CRM module if your PMS has one.

items.heading: Connected guest records
paragraphs: We connect the guest data in your PMS to your email platform through the platform's native integration or a scheduled export.

items.heading: Access and data protection
paragraphs: Your guest data stays in your systems. It's covered by your NDA or our data processing agreement, and that agreement is signed before we receive access.

blocks.heading: Client results

items.text: For a 34-room independent motel in Ontario, we rebuilt its OTA listings, fixed rate parity and launched direct-booking search campaigns. From March 2024 to February 2025 against the previous 12 months, its share of room nights booked direct rose from 9% to 21%, and its Booking.com content score (the extranet's own listing score) went from 62% to 100%.

blocks.heading: Working Directly With Owners and Their Teams

items.heading: Your dedicated specialist
paragraphs: Your specialist owns your account from start to finish and has at least 5 years' experience in independent and boutique hotel revenue and OTAs. They handle no more than 10 properties and are part of [our 12-person team](/about-us/), which provides coverage all 365 days of the year.

items.heading: Retail and leisure focus
paragraphs: We focus our marketing on retail and leisure direct bookings because that's where our work has the greatest effect. If groups, events or corporate contracts drive most of your revenue, we shape the work around supporting your director of sales.

items.heading: Group sales ownership
paragraphs: We advise on group strategy, and your director of sales runs group sales day to day. Those relationships and negotiations belong inside your hotel.

items.heading: Revenue Management Audit
paragraphs: We quote fixed-scope, fixed-fee [revenue management audits](/revenue-management-audit/) and roadmaps after your free 30-minute consultation. A standalone audit doesn't commit you to continuing. For a single property, you get the report within 10 business days of us receiving your data and access. For a group, add 10 business days for each batch of up to 5 properties.

blocks.heading: Direct Distribution That Wins Guests Back From OTAs

items.heading: Reasons to book direct
items.text: Guests who find you through OTAs need a clear advantage for booking direct and an easy checkout. We recommend breakfast, late check-out or flexible cancellation. We help you choose the ones your team can deliver consistently at a cost per stay that works for you.

items.heading: Booking engine setup
items.text: We draw on our experience with premium booking engines to select, configure and tune yours, so your direct-booking benefits stay clear all the way through checkout.

items.heading: Returning guest demand
items.text: We build your loyalty and repeat-guest programme and email past guests at the times they usually book to bring them back to you directly.

items.heading: Hotel Distribution
items.text: With [hotel distribution](/hotel-distribution/), we use booking trends and commissions to allocate your inventory across OTAs, GDS and direct channels. You keep your visibility on third-party sites while we control pricing and availability to reduce the risk of overbooking and preserve parity.

items.heading: OTA Optimization
items.text: Through [OTA optimization](/ota-optimization/), we refine your listings, rate plans and promotions, set up your channel-manager mapping, maintain parity, plan commissions and channel mix, and add metasearch and direct-booking links.

items.heading: Hotel Digital Marketing
items.text: As part of [hotel digital marketing](/hotel-digital-marketing/), we audit and optimise your existing website, or we build a new direct-booking website if you need one.

blocks.heading: Weeks 1 to 4: Diagnosing What Makes You Distinctive
paragraphs: In weeks 1 to 4, we base your positioning on booking evidence, not instinct.

steps.heading: Collect booking history
steps.text: You send us at least 12 months of booking history, or 24 months if you have it. Export it from your PMS by date, room type, channel and rate code.

steps.heading: Gather guest evidence
steps.text: We use whatever data you have on guest origins, lengths of stay, lead times and review scores, alongside competitive analysis and guest research.

steps.heading: Label missing evidence
steps.text: We fill any gaps with comp-set rates, market demand data and your budget. We mark these figures as estimates and revisit the diagnostic as your own data replaces them.

steps.heading: Identify distinctive strengths
steps.text: We compare your design, location, views and signature room types against your reviews and bookings to establish what guests value.

steps.heading: Define guest segments
steps.text: From the evidence we've collected, we identify 3 to 4 target segments, such as weekend couples or design-minded travellers.

steps.heading: Translate positioning into pricing
steps.text: We set base rates, rate floors and room-type differentials and price your distinctive rooms at a premium. We also match rate plans, minimum stays and packages to how each segment books.

blocks.heading: What We Need From You Before Kickoff

items.heading: Data access safeguards
paragraphs: Your data stays in your systems, and only our team has remote access to it. We keep our working files in access-controlled cloud storage that only our team can use. No subcontractor gets access to your account. Our [privacy policy](/privacy-policy/) sets out the details.

items.heading: Access and ownership
paragraphs: Before kickoff, you give us your property details, user access to your systems and the name of the person responsible for the work. If any access is missing, the timeline stalls.

items.heading: Calls and approvals
paragraphs: You join a 60-minute kickoff call, then remote working sessions every two weeks on Starter or every week on Core, and you reply to approval requests within 2 business days. Slow approvals delay delivery.

items.heading: No marketing person
paragraphs: If you don't have a marketing person, we train your general manager or a staff member you nominate. We can also act as your interim marketing lead until your new hire is trained.

blocks.heading: Weeks 5 to 10: Building Your Strategy and Pricing Framework
paragraphs: In weeks 5 to 10, we turn the diagnostic into an agreed foundation for the work that follows. You'll see less marketing activity early on. That's because launching channels and advertising before your rates and positioning are settled creates rework.

In this phase, we write your positioning and revenue strategy, set your pricing framework and agree both with you. Through our [Dynamic Pricing Strategy](/dynamic-pricing-strategy/), we also tune your gap-night rules and booking policies to local events and demand, and bring your budget under the same revenue strategy.

items.detail: Channel and marketing work begins in week 11, built on settled rates and positioning.

blocks.heading: Weeks 11 to 22: Direct Bookings, Paid Media and PR

items.heading: Distribution and visibility
paragraphs: In weeks 11 to 22, we optimise your direct bookings, calibrate your OTA presence, run paid acquisition where it's justified and handle PR and lifestyle media.

items.heading: Conversion before advertising
paragraphs: We only switch on paid channels once your booking engine converts at least 1.5% of visitors. Below that level, paid acquisition waits, and it doesn't start while conversion stays too low.

items.heading: Cost-based channel retention
paragraphs: We run a 60-day test budget. We keep a channel only if its cost per direct booking stays below the OTA commission you'd have paid on that booking.

items.heading: Paid channel selection
paragraphs: We use Google Hotel Ads, metasearch on Tripadvisor and Trivago, Google search ads on your brand and on high-intent searches, and Meta retargeting aimed at people who've already visited your website.

items.heading: Your account ownership
paragraphs: Your team opens the ad and metasearch accounts in your property's name, pays the platforms directly with your own payment method and gives us user access. This way, the data and history stay with you.

items.heading: PR materials and approvals
paragraphs: You give us a property fact sheet, 15 to 20 high-resolution photos and one contact who approves media requests within 2 business days.

blocks.heading: Final Weeks: Handing the Work to Your Team
paragraphs: Every consulting engagement ends with remote training and handover. In the final weeks, set aside time for your marketing, revenue, front office or sales staff to learn the routines over video call. Our documentation supports them as they learn.

We cover daily rate and restriction updates, weekly pace and pickup reviews, forecasting, OTA management, listing content and parity checks. Training also covers monthly occupancy, ADR and RevPAR reporting, plus your direct-booking and email marketing routines. After that, your team runs the work on its own. Our documentation stays with your team so they can keep those routines running.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you work with a boutique hotel that is still pre-opening or being repositioned, and has no booking history yet?
items.answer: Yes. We start up to 6 months before you open or relaunch, and we support your positioning, pricing, segmentation, distribution setup and early trading pace. If you don't have booking history or a mailing list yet, we work from comp-set rates, market demand and your budget. Your guest list grows from pre-opening sign-ups and early bookers. As your own booking data builds up, it replaces the estimates.

items.question: If I already have a marketing or PR agency, do you work alongside them or take over their scope?
items.answer: We work alongside your agency and don't take over its scope. At the start, we agree in writing who owns each channel, task and decision. Under that agreement, we lead revenue strategy, OTA distribution and direct-booking conversion, and your agency keeps creative, PR and campaign execution. We share monthly reports and join a monthly coordination call.

items.question: Can you reshape our direct and OTA distribution while retaining existing OTA, wholesaler and room-allotment agreements?
items.answer: Yes. We grow your direct bookings while using OTAs deliberately, and you don't drop any partners. Your existing contracts, allotments and negotiated corporate or wholesale rates stay in place unless you approve changes in writing.

items.question: How do you run guest research and the competitive analysis without visiting the property, and what data do you need from us?
items.answer: We run the whole diagnostic remotely, with no site visits. We compare you with 5 to 8 properties matched on location, type, size and price. For this we use daily competitor rate checks, booking pace, pickup, and live market data from pricing tools and OTA extranets. For guest research, we use the OTA reviews and PMS profiles you have, plus a short email survey sent to guests after their stay. From you, we need your property details, access to your systems and at least 12 months of booking history, or 24 months if you have it.

items.question: Does either consulting package include daily rate, restriction and inventory decisions, or must we retain that responsibility or purchase managed revenue services separately?
items.answer: No, neither consulting package includes those daily decisions. We build the strategy and pricing framework, and your team decides rates, restrictions and inventory. If you want us to make those daily decisions for every room type, we offer a separate monthly managed revenue management plan, which you can buy on its own or with consulting. You keep full control of your pricing, and we make major decisions together.

items.question: Can we remove or add parts of a package to fit what we need?
items.answer: Yes. You can drop PR, lifestyle media or paid acquisition. Instead of the standard channel count, you can choose one OTA channel or every channel you sell on. You can take revenue management, OTA management and related online services separately or together. If you combine them, we deliver them as a bundle with priority turnaround.

mainEntity.name: How does commercial strategy differ from your outsourced revenue management or revenue consulting in what you do, what our team does and what results we should expect?

acceptedAnswer.text: With commercial strategy, we set the direction with your leadership. With outsourced revenue management, we make the daily revenue decisions. With fixed-scope consulting, we give you an action plan for your existing revenue team to implement. Commercial strategy covers revenue management, marketing, sales and distribution, and it targets total revenue and channel profitability over a 12-month plan. With fully outsourced revenue management, your dedicated specialist decides daily rates, restrictions and inventory for every room type on a monthly retainer, and the target is day-to-day gains in occupancy, ADR and RevPAR. Fixed-scope consulting delivers an audit, a written report and a strategy roadmap. The right choice depends on whether someone in your organisation has the time and authority to act on pricing and commercial decisions. With commercial strategy, your team carries out the plan day to day, while we load the offers we design; system setup carries its own fixed fee. To get started, you share access and data and we plan with your leadership. After that come ongoing strategy calls and approvals.

mainEntity.name: Can you build a commercial strategy for a newly opened or repositioned property without representative trading history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If you don't have representative trading history, we build your commercial strategy from competitive-set rates, market demand data and your budget. Then we switch to your own data as bookings build. We pick 5 to 8 comparable properties that match your new location, type, size and price level. During the first 12 months, we revisit the strategy with you every 6 to 8 weeks, until your own history can lead decisions.

mainEntity.name: Does your ancillary-revenue work include setting prices and designing packages or upsell offers, or only identifying opportunities for our team?

acceptedAnswer.text: It includes setting prices, designing packages and upsell offers, and loading them into your systems. We don't stop at identifying opportunities. We price add-ons such as parking, breakfast and early check-in, design room packages and pre-arrival upsell offers, and load them as rate plans in your booking engine, PMS and OTA extranets. Your team approves each offer and delivers the service at the property. We don't run hotel operations. Each month, we report take-up and revenue for every offer.

mainEntity.name: How do you determine whether our commercial goals require a new system rather than better use of tools we already license?

acceptedAnswer.text: We recommend a new system only in two cases: your commercial goal can't be met by reconfiguring your existing tools or making full use of them, or the workaround would cost your team more than 5 hours a week. First, we audit how your PMS, channel manager, RMS and CRM are configured and used. Then we map each goal to features you already license. We don't accept referral commissions from software vendors or OTAs, so we base our recommendation only on what fits your property.

Fixed-scope consulting delivers an audit, a written report and a strategy roadmap. The right choice depends on whether someone in your organisation has the time and authority to act on pricing and commercial decisions. With commercial strategy, your team carries out the plan day to day, while we load the offers we design; system setup carries its own fixed fee. To get started, you share access and data and we plan with your leadership. After that come ongoing strategy calls and approvals.

items.question: Can you build a commercial strategy for a newly opened or repositioned property without representative trading history?
items.answer: Yes. If you don't have representative trading history, we build your commercial strategy from competitive-set rates, market demand data and your budget. Then we switch to your own data as bookings build. We pick 5 to 8 comparable properties that match your new location, type, size and price level. During the first 12 months, we revisit the strategy with you every 6 to 8 weeks, until your own history can lead decisions.

items.question: Does your ancillary-revenue work include setting prices and designing packages or upsell offers, or only identifying opportunities for our team?
items.answer: It includes setting prices, designing packages and upsell offers, and loading them into your systems. We don't stop at identifying opportunities. We price add-ons such as parking, breakfast and early check-in, design room packages and pre-arrival upsell offers, and load them as rate plans in your booking engine, PMS and OTA extranets. Your team approves each offer and delivers the service at the property. We don't run hotel operations. Each month, we report take-up and revenue for every offer.

items.question: How do you determine whether our commercial goals require a new system rather than better use of tools we already license?
items.answer: We recommend a new system only in two cases: your commercial goal can't be met by reconfiguring your existing tools or making full use of them, or the workaround would cost your team more than 5 hours a week. First, we audit how your PMS, channel manager, RMS and CRM are configured and used. Then we map each goal to features you already license. We don't accept referral commissions from software vendors or OTAs, so we base our recommendation only on what fits your property.

items.question: My property is not listed on Expedia or Agoda yet. Can you create and launch new listings for me, or do you only rebuild listings that already exist?
items.answer: Yes. We launch new Expedia, Agoda and regional listings, starting from the application and registration, and we create the accounts in your property's name. items.question: Can I limit the engagement to selected channels, for example only Booking.com and Expedia, and add others later?
items.answer: Yes. You choose the channels, and you can add others later. We recommend starting with the ones that already bring you the most bookings. Each extra launch is one-off setup work, and we quote it before it starts. Your monthly retainer stays the same.

items.question: Can you restrict your work to listing content and distribution while our existing revenue manager retains all base-rate and stay-restriction decisions?
items.answer: Yes. With standalone OTA management, we cover content, rate plan structure, promotions, parity and channel manager settings, and your revenue manager keeps every base-rate and stay-restriction decision. We agree in writing who owns which channels and tasks. We never change your revenue manager's rates or restrictions. When we spot an issue, we flag it for them to decide.

items.question: Can you manage several OTA accounts directly if we have no channel manager, or is installing one a prerequisite?
items.answer: Yes. We work directly in each extranet and update rates, availability and content by hand. We use named logins, and you remove them when we finish. You don't need a channel manager. items.question: Will you talk to my Booking.com, Expedia or Agoda market managers on my behalf about commission, programme terms or contract conditions?
items.answer: Yes. We negotiate those matters with your market managers and push for performance incentives or volume-based commission reductions. You approve every proposal first, and you sign any new contract yourself.

items.question: Do you commit to any target for ranking, conversion or booking share, and what do you do if the 30-day review shows no improvement?

You keep the right to cancel at the end of any month.

blocks.heading: A Dynamic Pricing Strategy Benchmarked Against Your Comp Set
paragraphs: Before pricing starts, you review the competitive set we'll benchmark your dynamic pricing strategy against: 5 to 8 comparable properties. Once you've agreed it, that comparison guides your setup and, on our managed levels, our daily rate checks; after a self-run setup, your team runs those checks.

blocks.heading: Who RateHarbor Is and How We Forecast Demand
paragraphs: We build your demand calendar 12 months ahead from at least 12 months of your booking history, or 24 months if you have it. We combine your booking patterns with market evidence to classify demand, and we revise the calendar as new signals appear.

Some events are announced late and others never appear on public calendars, so the calendar is a working document rather than a fixed forecast. If your booking history is short or patchy, your initial calendar is less reliable and leans more heavily on market data.

As your [outsourced hotel revenue and OTA management company](/about-us/), RateHarbor assigns you one dedicated specialist from our 12-person team. Your specialist has at least 5 years of experience with independent and boutique hotels. Each specialist handles no more than 10 properties, and the team covers you all 365 days of the year.

Shows the order in which the demand calendar is built, rated and kept up to date.

items.label: Gather booking and market data
items.detail: Booking history, pace and pickup, daily competitor rates and live market data from your pricing tools and OTA extranets.

items.label: Find local events
items.detail: City event calendars, convention centre schedules, public and school holidays and sudden rate jumps across your competitive set.

items.label: Rate each date
items.detail: Each date is rated low, normal, high or peak demand by its expected effect on occupancy and competitor rates.

items.label: Re-rate as signals appear
items.detail: Dates are re-rated as soon as competitor rates or booking pace show an event not yet logged.

blocks.heading: Tracking Results Against Your Competitive Set
paragraphs: If your hotel subscribes to paid market-share data, we track three indexes from it against your competitive set: occupancy (MPI), ADR (ARI) and RevPAR (RGI). Without that data, we compare competitor rates, booking pace and pickup instead, and label those comparisons as estimates, never as MPI, ARI or RGI. Managed levels show them in weekly and monthly reports and an in-depth quarterly review. An index at your competitive set's level means you're matching it, and a higher index means you're gaining share.

We judge pricing mainly by how those measures move, not by occupancy or ADR alone. We compare your results with the same period last year and with your budget, which separates pricing performance from seasonality and wider market movement. That's why managed levels review and update your competitive set with you every quarter, and a self-run setup at each paid revisit.

blocks.heading: What Every Hotel Pricing Setup Includes

items.heading: Room-type foundations
paragraphs: Every room type gets its own base rate and floor, set against where your property stands within the competitive set.

items.heading: Cost-based floors
paragraphs: We calculate floors before adding any rules. They cover housekeeping, laundry, amenities, utilities and the minimum margin you choose. If floors are set only against competitors, bookings from expensive channels are exposed to returns below what they cost to service.

items.heading: Channel-safe returns
paragraphs: We gross up floors for your highest channel commission and payment fees, so your minimum net return is protected on every channel. On very weak nights, these floors keep you priced above distressed competitors, so you never sell a room below what it costs to service.

items.heading: Demand-responsive rates
paragraphs: Each room type's rate levels move with that room type's own occupancy and booking pace. We don't treat all categories alike.

items.heading: Protected category gaps
paragraphs: We link higher categories to your reference room by a fixed amount or percentage and keep at least the minimum gap you approve. Categories that fill faster climb further, but an upgrade never prices at or below the category beneath it.

items.heading: Booking controls
paragraphs: Your pricing setup includes lead-time and last-minute rules, minimum and maximum stays, and closed-to-arrival and closed-to-departure controls.

items.heading: Longer stays and packages
paragraphs: Pricing for longer stays and packages is a core part of the strategy we deliver to you.

items.heading: Separate channel markups
paragraphs: We set separate markups for OTAs, GDS and your direct channel instead of using one markup across all channels.

items.question: Can you build a pricing strategy for a newly opened property with little booking history, and what evidence would you use instead?
items.answer: Yes. Instead of past bookings, we start with competitive-set rates, market demand data and your budget. As your bookings build up, we move over to your own pace and pickup. If you book revisits, usually every 6 to 8 weeks, we refine the strategy at each one.

items.question: My hotel doesn't use PriceLabs. Can you still build the strategy live in my own system, or do I need to set up a pricing tool first?
items.answer: Yes. We build live in the pricing tool or RMS you already use, such as Beyond Pricing. We can also build in your PMS or channel-manager rate settings, such as Cloudbeds or SiteMinder. The session runs 90 minutes to 3 hours. It covers floors, base rates, BAR tiers, seasonal and event changes, stay restrictions, length-of-stay rules and channel markups. You don't need a replacement system or a dynamic pricing tool. If you want a tool, we recommend one that fits your property, and we take no vendor referral commissions. We set it up before the session.

items.question: Can you keep our negotiated corporate, group and wholesale rates outside dynamic adjustments while pricing publicly available rooms dynamically?
items.answer: Yes. We load your negotiated rates as fixed plans that aren't linked to BAR. We keep those rates and their allotments out of dynamic adjustments and change them only with your written approval. Your public rooms stay dynamically priced. If a contracted rate is more than 15% below BAR on a high-demand date, we flag it for your next contract-renewal review.

items.question: If our team manually changes a rate or restriction, how do you prevent the managed pricing process from overwriting that change unintentionally?
items.answer: We never overwrite your manual rate or restriction changes. Our daily review flags and logs each override. We then lock that date and room type in your pricing tool, so the automation skips it. We discuss it with you on your next strategy call, and it stays in place until you approve removing it.

items.question: How do you prevent or reverse inappropriate rate changes when booking data becomes stale or a pricing integration fails?
items.answer: If booking data goes more than 12 hours without refreshing, we hold rates at their last verified levels and apply your floors. A sync or integration failure triggers an alert; we suspend automated updates and protect affected OTA availability. We fix faults on our side within 4 hours and tell you that day. A PMS, channel manager or OTA fault we find, report and coordinate; its fix time is that provider's. We restore mistaken rates from the change log that day and reconcile reservations with your PMS within 24 hours of syncing resuming. A second specialist reviews every automated rule change before it goes live. Your team loads any bookings we flag as missing.

items.heading: Systems and reporting
paragraphs: We check how your PMS, CRS, RMS, channel manager and business-intelligence tools are set up and used, including your data quality and reporting accuracy.

items.heading: Revenue governance
paragraphs: We look at your meeting frequency, decision rights, responsibilities and standard operating procedures, then check whether the revenue actions you agree are actually carried through.

items.heading: Record reconciliation
paragraphs: Before we draw any conclusions, we reconcile your PMS, channel manager, OTA extranet and financial records, and we flag every figure we can't verify.

items.heading: Missing data limits
paragraphs: When evidence is missing, it limits what we can conclude about forecast accuracy, net channel contribution and year-on-year trends. Your pricing, rate structures, restrictions and system setup stay fully reviewable.

items.heading: PriceLabs setup
paragraphs: If you already have a PriceLabs setup, our [Dynamic Pricing Strategy service](/dynamic-pricing-strategy/) audits it for leakage and missed growth opportunities, and that takes 1 to 2 business days.

items.heading: Distribution implementation
paragraphs: Our [Hotel Distribution service](/hotel-distribution/) allocates your inventory across OTAs, GDS and direct channels based on booking trends and commissions, and it controls your rates and availability to maintain parity and reduce overbooking risk.

blocks.heading: Profitability Audit: Margins, Acquisition Costs and Net Contribution

items.heading: Commercial profitability
items.text: We work out what it costs you to win each booking and what each channel, segment and revenue source contributes net. We then check those figures against the rooms revenue lines in your P&L.

items.heading: Direct acquisition costs
items.text: OTA commissions, payment fees, brand and loyalty fees, and paid campaign spend are charged directly to the channel or segment that incurs them.

items.heading: Shared cost allocation
items.text: Some marketing, distribution and sales costs can't be traced to one channel. We split those by share of room-nights or room revenue, using the method we agree with you at scoping.

items.heading: Transparent contribution calculations
items.text: We show allocated costs separately, next to gross revenue and net contribution, so you can test a different split yourself.

items.heading: Commercial contract terms
items.text: We review your commercial contracts together with your marketing spend, distribution costs and sales costs to see how they affect your margins.

items.heading: Reporting and alignment
items.text: We look at how much visibility your P&L gives you, how good your ownership reporting is and how well aligned your commercial teams are.

items.heading: Growth business cases
items.text: We check that each revenue-growth initiative has a clear business case that's measured against profit, not just revenue.

items.heading: Operating cost boundary
items.text: We don't run hotel operations, and we don't audit payroll, utilities, food costs or staffing. General operating costs are left out of the channel calculations, but we flag GOP constraints.

steps.heading: Agree the scope
steps.text: We confirm your priorities and challenges with you and settle whether the audit covers revenue management, profitability or both.

steps.heading: Review the evidence
steps.text: Our experts review and analyse your performance data, reports, systems, processes, documentation and commercial strategies.

steps.heading: Validate with stakeholders
steps.text: We interview your stakeholders so we understand the context. In those interviews we challenge assumptions and test the opportunities we've found before we present them.

steps.heading: Present the recommendations
steps.text: We walk you through our findings and prioritised recommendations, along with a roadmap that shows your team what to tackle first.

blocks.heading: Data, Access and Time Needed From Your Team
paragraphs: Send us your property details and at least 12 months of booking history. If you have 24 months, send all 24. Break down reservations, room revenue and rates by date, room type, channel and rate plan. We also ask for your P&L, your current budget and forecast, and your competitive-set reports. If your property is newly opened and has no booking history, we work from competitive-set rates, market demand data and your budget instead.

Give each of our specialists a named login to your PMS, channel manager, RMS and OTA extranets, set at the lowest permission level the task needs. Your team will need to give us a 60-minute kickoff call plus remote video interviews of about 45 minutes each with up to 4 stakeholders. That comes to about 4 to 6 hours in total.

items.question: Is this audit the same as the revenue audit you do at the start of a managed engagement, or is it a separate, deeper paid engagement?

items.question: Can you complete the audit using read-only access or data exports without permission to change our live rates and system settings?
items.answer: Yes. We work from read-only logins or exports from your PMS, RMS, channel manager and OTA extranets, and we have no permission to change your live rates or settings. Each of our specialists gets their own named login with the lowest permissions the work needs. We never use a shared password. We stop using your systems on the last day and confirm this in writing within 5 business days. You then remove our logins.

items.question: How many weeks does a Revenue Management Audit, a Profitability Audit or a combined audit take from start to final presentation?
items.answer: For a single property, each format takes 3 to 4 weeks from scoping to the management presentation. We deliver the written report within 10 business days of receiving your data and access. Each additional batch of up to 5 group properties adds 10 business days. Data collection and stakeholder interviews take the longest, and data collection moves as fast as you send us your exports and logins. We schedule the interviews within the first week of the review.

items.question: After you deliver the roadmap, can you help us put it into action or check our progress later?
items.answer: Yes. We offer implementation support with a fixed scope, which we quote separately, and video training your team can work through at its own pace. You can book a follow-up KPI review. You can also move to monthly management, and the audit then serves as the discovery step. Every consulting engagement ends with remote training and a handover to your staff.

items.question: Do we receive editable analysis files and calculation assumptions that our own team can inspect and update, or only the finished report and presentation?
items.answer: You get both. Along with the finished report and presentation, you receive editable supporting spreadsheets. They record every calculation assumption and data source, so your team can check and update the figures. You own all the reports and files we create. We hand over the documentation and files within 10 business days after the engagement ends.

items.question: Can you audit our revenue management when a brand or external operator controls pricing, contracts or system access, and what would remain outside your review?
items.answer: Yes. We hold the pricing, forecasting, distribution and reporting your provider controls to the same standards we use for our own work. We work from the reports, exports and read-only access the provider gives us, and we mark which areas they control. Our conclusions leave out brand rate programmes we can't see, central reservation rules, corporate or wholesale contracts that haven't been disclosed to us, and the provider's internal decisions. We list these exclusions so you can raise them with the provider. The audit is a standalone job, and you aren't committed to any further work. We don't accept referral fees from OTAs or software vendors, and we recommend only what suits your property. We also point out the arrangements that should stay as they are.

mainEntity.name: How does this work for a seasonal property that closes for part of the year?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you're closed, we pause daily pricing. We still check your listings and reply to new reviews every month. We close off-season dates on every channel. We also set opening rates and minimum stays based on past seasons, comp-set rates and market demand, so guests can book up to 12 months ahead. Full pricing starts again 8 weeks before you reopen.

mainEntity.name: How do you work alongside a revenue manager or front desk staff I already have?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the start, we agree in writing who owns which channels and tasks. Your staff keep check-in, guest service, walk-ins and direct bookings. We handle pricing, restrictions and OTA listings remotely. We email you the current rate plan, and we email every change on the day it goes live. At launch, we also give a 30-minute remote briefing. That keeps your staff and channels aligned with minimal disruption.

mainEntity.name: Who makes the final call on rates, you or me?

acceptedAnswer.text: You keep full control of pricing. We make major decisions together, and you can see every rate and channel while we keep disruption to your team to a minimum.

mainEntity.name: What do you do between reviews if something sudden happens, like a local event or a drop in bookings?

acceptedAnswer.text: We check rates every day and change prices in real time. We base those changes on demand, booking pace, live pickup, seasonality, events, competitor benchmarks and market trends. On the monthly retainer, we decide rates, restrictions and inventory for every room type and revise the strategy as conditions change. When demand is slow, we use targeted tactics to fill unsold rooms. At peak demand, the aim shifts to the highest ADR the market will accept. We check your OTAs every day for slower bookings and broken rate parity, track your listings' ranking every week, and fix any problem we find.

items.heading: Continuity and fit
paragraphs: Your specialist keeps track of your property's demand context, so decisions stay consistent. When they're away, our team covers so pricing carries on. If the relationship isn't working, ask for a replacement early so the mismatch doesn't drag on.

paragraphs: On the monthly retainer, [Dynamic Pricing Strategy](/dynamic-pricing-strategy/) means we manage daily rates, restrictions and inventory for every room type and adjust them to live demand and market conditions.

blocks.heading: Remote Work Inside Your Existing Systems
paragraphs: We work remotely inside the PMS, channel manager and RMS you already use, through our own logins, so you don't need replacement software. We don't have on-site staff at any property.

Staying with your current systems means you avoid the rate and inventory risks and the staff retraining that come with switching mid-season. The value comes from our decisions, not from a new tool. What your systems can do sets the limit: if your setup is restricted, some automation isn't possible until you upgrade.

blocks.heading: Reports, Strategy Calls and Your Control Over Rates

items.heading: Weekly and monthly performance reviews
paragraphs: We walk your team through the results on your weekly or monthly strategy call. Owners and GMs get weekly and monthly reports covering RevPAR growth, occupancy trends, ADR movement, visibility, revenue and forecast accuracy.

items.heading: Leadership reporting
paragraphs: Our monthly report sets out the key performance metrics, and every quarter you get an in-depth review. Senior leadership also gets regular financial performance reports and forecasts.

items.heading: Live KPI access
paragraphs: Live dashboards let you check occupancy, ADR, RevPAR and channel mix at any time, so you can see how you're performing between reviews.

items.heading: Strategy call schedule
paragraphs: We hold strategy calls weekly or monthly to go over results and direction. More frequent calls and reports take up more owner and GM time, so we set the schedule to match how involved your leadership wants to be.

items.heading: Your pricing control
paragraphs: You keep full control of pricing and can see every rate and channel. We make major decisions together with you and keep disruption to your team to a minimum.

items.heading: Check before signing
paragraphs: Before you sign, we send you an anonymised sample monthly report. Look at how it explains rate changes, results and forecasts against actuals, not just the KPIs. That shows you how you'll hold us accountable.

items.heading: Sample daily snapshot
paragraphs: You also get a sample daily snapshot. It shows changes from the last 24 hours, a day-by-day view of the next 12 months and competitors' rates for context.

blocks.heading: What We Need From You: Input, Approvals and Access
paragraphs: Name one contact who approves quickly. Join weekly or monthly strategy calls, answer approvals within 2 business days and keep active named logins for your PMS, channel manager, RMS and OTA extranets; lapsed access or late approvals stop work. Give us 14 days' notice of renovations, rooms out of service, group blocks, events or budget changes.
Our [data handling policy](/privacy-policy/) follows PIPEDA, plus GDPR and UK GDPR where they apply.

items.heading: Checklist and turnaround
paragraphs: At the start, we send you an access and data checklist. Once it's complete, we finish most quick services within 1 to 3 business days. Most delays come from waiting for property details and access.

items.heading: One-time scope
paragraphs: A one-time service gives you a snapshot of your property. It doesn't include ongoing adjustments as demand changes.

items.heading: Commercial Strategy consulting
paragraphs: If you already have a revenue team and want an outside view, [Commercial Strategy](/commercial-strategy/) gives you fixed-scope consulting. That means a written revenue audit, a custom roadmap, pricing and distribution strategy, and market positioning analysis that includes your competitive set.

steps.text: Before any engagement, you get a [free 30-minute consultation and free quote](/request-a-quote/), and you don't have to commit to going ahead.

steps.heading: Audit before targets
steps.text: After you sign, before we set goals or estimate the work, we look at your pricing, channel mix, OTA positioning, past performance and competitive set. Your rates stay as they are during discovery.

steps.heading: Agree the strategy
steps.text: Working from your property data, we agree goals, estimate the time and any third-party costs and build the strategy. Our fees stay as signed; scope changes need your written approval.

steps.heading: Phase group delivery
steps.text: For multi-property groups, we start with one representative property. Then we roll out in batches and use what we've learned along the way. Later properties wait until their batch comes up.

mainEntity.name: How often are the guides and checklists updated?

acceptedAnswer.text: We review every guide and checklist each quarter. Whenever Booking.com or Expedia changes its listing or ranking rules, we update the OTA listing checklist within 30 days. Outdated guidance can harm your visibility, so always use the latest version.

mainEntity.name: Can I adapt the templates and share them with my staff?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can edit any template, add your own room types and figures, and share it with staff and general managers at every property you run. You can't resell the files or republish them as your own.

mainEntity.name: Do I need any particular software to open or use the templates?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you don't need any special software. The templates are Excel (.xlsx) files that open in Excel, Google Sheets, Apple Numbers and LibreOffice. The guides and checklists are PDFs that open in any browser. You don't need any new systems, and there are no setup costs. The templates aren't connected to a PMS, channel manager or pricing tool, so you enter or paste your figures by hand. The more properties you have, the more work this takes.

mainEntity.name: Can I ask someone a question if a guide doesn't fit my property?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Send our team an enquiry about your property and the guide. We'll answer your question about the guide.

paragraphs: We walk you through base rates, rate floors, seasonal and event adjustments, and length-of-stay rules so you can make pricing decisions for your property. Its first section sets a rate floor from your cost per occupied room.

paragraphs: The checklist covers your titles, descriptions, photos, room types, policies and rate parity on Booking.com and Expedia, with checks such as "Same rate and policy on both sites for this date and room?"

items.heading: Annual budget template
paragraphs: We break your annual budget down by month and by segment, so you can work from either view: months run across, segments down, with room nights, ADR and room revenue.

items.heading: Monthly performance report
paragraphs: The report tracks occupancy, ADR, RevPAR and channel mix. When you use it alongside the rate guide, you measure your pricing decisions and your results against the same figures. Each month you can see whether your rules are doing what you set them up to do.

items.heading: Monthly time commitment
paragraphs: To use the paired tools properly, someone who knows your property's numbers has to spend time on them every month. If you run a very small property without a dedicated manager, keeping up that commitment is harder.

blocks.heading: How to Get Each Resource & When to Use It

items.text: Use the rate strategy guide 8 to 12 weeks before your peak season, because that's when it's most useful.

items.heading: Year-round demand
items.text: If your demand is fairly even with no clear peak, seasonal timing gives you less value. In that case, review your rates on a steady rolling schedule.

items.text: Go through the OTA listing checklist before any listing refresh and use it to guide your changes.

seo.title: Careers: Roles, Team Life & How to Apply | RateHarbor
seo.description: Find out what joining RateHarbor offers: the roles we hire for, how our team works day to day and the steps from application to offer. Explore careers.

mainEntity.name: Do you hire people with no experience in the hotel industry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. For owner reporting analyst and junior OTA roles, you don't need hotel industry experience as long as you have at least 2 years of work in data analysis, e-commerce or online marketing. We train you over your first 3 months. Specialist roles that own client accounts are different: for those, you need at least 5 years of hands-on hotel revenue management or OTA experience.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer internships or student placements?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each year we offer up to 2 paid remote placements for students in hospitality, tourism, business or data analytics programmes, and each one lasts 3 to 6 months. You work alongside a specialist on competitive set monitoring, listing content and performance reports for hotels, motels, B&Bs, serviced apartments and short-term rentals.

mainEntity.name: Will you keep my application on file if no role fits right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if you ask for this in the note with your CV. We keep it only to consider you for future roles, and if a role that matches your experience opens, we contact you directly. You can ask us to update or delete your application at any time, and we act on your request within 5 business days.

mainEntity.name: How do you set salaries and review pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: When we advertise an open role, its posting includes the salary range. With no open role, your application joins our talent pool, and we tell you the range before any interview. We set pay by level across three bands: associate, specialist and senior, and an offer sits within that range. Fixed bands support fair pay across our remote team. The trade-off is that you have less room to negotiate. If you're based in Canada, we pay you in Canadian dollars. If you're on the remote team somewhere else, we pay you in your local currency, so take-home pay isn't identical from one country to another. We review pay for everyone on the team every 12 months.

hero.heading: Careers at RateHarbor
lead: Join a fully remote team where you own real results for hotel owners.

blocks.heading: Why Join RateHarbor?
paragraphs: You'll join a 12-person team that works fully remotely. You own results for hotel owners, and you work inside each client's own systems. We provide revenue management, OTA management and owner reporting for independent hotels and small hotel groups in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and other countries. We're looking for people who enjoy working with hotel data and online channels.

blocks.heading: How Our Remote Team Works
paragraphs: The team has three groups: revenue management, OTA management and owner reporting. Each account has one dedicated specialist, so owners always deal with someone they know. When you're on vacation or in training, colleagues who know the account cover your properties. Pricing and listings need attention every day, so part of your week goes on handover notes and shared updates. Some people find this coordination work less rewarding than direct client work.

Your core hours are 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday to Friday. You get 20 paid vacation days a year and weekly internal training and knowledge-sharing sessions. We also give you paid time to take revenue management certification courses.

blocks.heading: The Roles We Hire For
paragraphs: Our roles all cover the same properties, but each is narrower than a generalist hotel job. Pick the one matching your strongest interest; you'll serve clients better.

items.heading: Revenue Management Specialists
paragraphs: This is the role for you if you want to own pricing decisions. You handle pricing and rate strategy, demand forecasting and daily competitive set checks, and you own up to 10 client properties from start to finish.

items.heading: OTA Management Specialists
paragraphs: This is the role for you if you want to work on channel operations. You run listings, content, rate parity and channel manager settings on Booking.com, Expedia and other online travel agencies.

items.heading: Owner Reporting Analysts
paragraphs: This is the role for you if you want to turn performance data into reports. You build weekly and monthly owner reports covering occupancy, ADR and RevPAR.

blocks.heading: How to Apply: From Application to Offer
paragraphs: Job titles vary, so we judge your practical work, not just your CV, across three video-call steps over about 3 weeks.

steps.heading: Practical Property Exercise
steps.text: You spend 2 hours on pricing or listings for a sample property. These 2 hours show us how you work more clearly than an interview answer does.

steps.heading: Final Team Interview
steps.text: After you finish the practical exercise, you meet two team members for the final interview.

steps.heading: Decision Or Offer
steps.text: Within 5 business days of the final interview, we send you a decision or a written offer.

mainEntity.name: What should I send if my property is new and has no recent performance figures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Send us your room count, room types, opening date, budget and any bookings you already have. If you have no booking history, we build your proposal from competitor-set rates and market demand data, and we price from those sources and your budget. As reservations come in, we switch to your own booking data. Pricing in the first months is less precise and needs closer review. Once a property has booking history, its pricing is more precise because it's based on its own data.

mainEntity.name: Can I ask for one proposal covering several properties?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Just list each property's type, room count and location in a single request. We work with hotels, motels, B&Bs, serviced apartments and short-term rentals. Each property is priced in its own room-count tier, and we deliver the work in batches. You get one document that sets out the scope, fees and start order for each property.

mainEntity.name: Can I see a sample proposal before I send my details?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Before you share your details, we can email you an anonymised sample proposal. If you ask, we also send an anonymised monthly performance report, full case studies for you to review before you sign.

mainEntity.name: Will you visit the property before you write the proposal?

lead: Send your property details and booking history, and we return a proposal built on your numbers.

blocks.heading: What to Send for an Exact Proposal
paragraphs: To get an exact proposal, send us your property details along with at least 12 months of booking history, or 24 months if you have it. For that period, your revenue management proposal needs your monthly occupancy, ADR and RevPAR, plus your channel mix across OTAs and direct bookings. Please also include your room count, room types, current rate plans, channel manager and the 3 to 5 competitors you watch. That lets us set the right room-count tier and scope.
